title: Cargo Compartment Lining Panels — Removal

issue.reason: Original issue of the cargo compartment lining panel removal task.

abstract: Removal of cargo compartment lining panels for panel replacement, covering both the clip-mounted light strip standard and the standard where the light assembly is carried inside the panel.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of the lining panels from a cargo compartment for panel replacement, and identifies the different disconnection sequence that applies where the compartment light strip is carried inside the panel.
sections.job_setup_note: The compartment must be empty and the cargo nets and loading rail covers must be removed first. The light connection sequence depends on the panel standard: on the recessed standard the light connector is behind the panel and has to be released before the panel can come clear, so the panel must not be pulled. Establish the fitted panel standard before work starts.
sections.procedure: 1. WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT THE CARGO DOOR IS SAFE AGAINST INADVERTENT CLOSING BEFORE ANY PERSON WORKS IN THE COMPARTMENT. 2. Empty the compartment and remove the cargo nets and the loading rail covers. 3. Establish the fitted panel standard and record it. 4. On the clip-mounted standard, disconnect the light strip at the exposed connector and remove the strip from its clips. 5. CAUTION: ON THE RECESSED STANDARD DO NOT PULL THE PANEL. THE LIGHT CONNECTOR IS BEHIND IT AND WILL BE DAMAGED. 6. On the recessed standard, release the panel fasteners, ease the panel forward by 30 mm only and release the light connector behind it. 7. Release the anchor nut fasteners EN513769-76 at each panel position. 8. Remove the panel and put it on the padded rack; do not stack panels face to face. 9. Examine the frame brackets and the exposed lower shell and record any finding. 10. Examine the light assembly D2550118482429 for damage to the lens and to the connector. 11. Identify each panel with its position before it leaves the compartment. 12. Protect the smoke detector sampling points against contamination while the compartment is open.
sections.close_out: Make sure that the smoke detector sampling points are protected and that no fastener is left loose in the compartment. Record the panel standard, the panel positions removed and any structural finding in the aircraft technical record.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. The recessed light strip disconnection sequence applies only to aircraft at the impact resistant panel standard.

safety_precautions: Make sure that the cargo door is safe against inadvertent closing.
Protect the smoke detector sampling points while the compartment is open.
Do not stack lining panels face to face.

title: Cargo Compartment Lining Panels — Removal

issue.reason: Task declared as the single access sequence for structural work behind the lining, with the panel standard recorded for the sealing procedure that calls it.

abstract: Removal of cargo compartment lining panels, covering both the clip-mounted light strip standard and the standard where the light assembly is carried inside the panel and is connected behind it.

sections.purpose: This task gives the removal of the lining panels from a cargo compartment, and identifies the different disconnection sequence that applies where the compartment light strip is carried inside the panel. It is the only access sequence for the lower shell and the sill behind the lining, and structural tasks that need that access call this task rather than repeating it.

Establish the fitted panel standard before work starts. Where the panels are being taken out to reach the longitudinal joint rather than to change a panel, agree the panel positions with the structural work package first, because only the positions over the worked bays need to come out and each one adds an hour to the job.
